mkdir -p /home/wlia0047/ar57/wenyu/GeneRec/results/research/issue121/rounds/round_20261026_030226_517/agents/scoring_2_retry1 && cat > /home/wlia0047/ar57/wenyu/GeneRec/results/research/issue121/rounds/round_20261026_030226_517/agents/scoring_2_retry1/scores_retry.txt <<'EOF'
SCORE: beh_ranked_hyp_tail | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: beh_ranked_hyp_tail | IN_SCOPE | Train-only outgoing transitions produce b_i; b_i directly changes level-3 Poincare assignment through a code bias, and comparisons include behavior-off, Euclidean, and both-on as specified.
EVIDENCE: beh_ranked_hyp_tail | E1 E2 E5 E12 E13 E14 E15 E6 E7 E16 E17
OBJECTION: beh_ranked_hyp_tail | The scalar is standardized log outdegree, not successor identity or successor-community choice; code-specific biases may mostly sort popularity, and post-fit collision ranks cannot establish that the assignment improved recommendation.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: beh_ranked_hyp_tail | Two items with identical outdegree but disjoint successor sets receive identical b_i, so the claimed signal cannot distinguish their continuation communities.
RATIONALE: beh_ranked_hyp_tail | E5 supports a measured, strongly varying successor-entropy problem, but does not validate this outdegree proxy or its coverage for the exact signal, so behavior=3. Poincare distance is genuinely used in assignment, yet the code bias could be duplicated by a Euclidean assignment bias and no cancellation/necessity argument is supplied (geometry=3). The computation differs from measured successor-geodesic coarse and tangent residual methods (E6-E7), but prior-art search is NOT_CHECKED (E16), so novelty=3. Changing q3 changes the three-token SID and the proposal names T3/T4 and Stage3 observables (downstream=4). Controls are mentioned, but matched settings and a concrete failure threshold/diagnostic are incomplete (falsifiability=2). The straight-through tail-count gradient, occupied-child min/max and categorical assignment details are underspecified, and training-cost estimate is not enough to resolve them (implementability=2). It is a distinct, testable mechanism with an informative popularity-versus-transition failure mode (exploration=3). UNKNOWN: exact control matching and tail-loss gradient implementation; bounded check: implement one fixed-seed batch and verify gradient, occupied-child behavior, and equal-budget ablations.

SCORE: beh_curvature_prefix_margin | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: beh_curvature_prefix_margin | IN_SCOPE | Train-only directed successor profiles determine item curvature used in level-3 Poincare assignment and the same prefix-conditioned computation; includes behavior-off and Euclidean comparisons.
EVIDENCE: beh_curvature_prefix_margin | E1 E2 E5 E12 E13 E14 E15 E16 E6 E7
OBJECTION: beh_curvature_prefix_margin | The specified P_i normalization is only over observed successors, while the stated +1e-3 smoothing and denominator are ambiguous; low-degree items can therefore have unstable entropy/curvature and pair eligibility.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: beh_curvature_prefix_margin | For a row with one observed successor, normalized entropy is zero regardless of how little evidence supports that edge; it receives the same extreme low-curvature setting as a well-supported deterministic row.
RATIONALE: beh_curvature_prefix_margin | Train entropy has measured stratification and broad reported item support in E5, but its exact pairwise overlap statistics/coverage for this use are not established, so behavior=3. Item-dependent Poincare distance and curvature affect assignment and margin geometry; matched Euclidean control is named, but no argument rules out a matched transform reproducing the effect (geometry=3). It combines known successor-geodesic/tangent families (E6-E7) in a distinct curvature-and-prefix-margin route; prior-art search is not present in the bundle, limiting novelty=3. The proposed chain changes q3, prefix representatives, continuation survival and named Stage3 metric (downstream=4). The behavior-off, geometry-off/Euclidean, both-on comparison is described and the retain criterion is stated, though no precise falsification threshold or diagnostic separating curvature from margin is supplied (falsifiability=3). Differentiable maps are plausible, but curvature convention for each pair, sparse overlap normalization, guards and full cost for sparse degree are not sufficiently pinned down (implementability=2). Distinct enough to test the interaction and failure of entropy-conditioned curvature is informative (exploration=3). UNKNOWN: exact Euclidean match and pair-sampling/evaluation thresholds; bounded check: run a fixed batch numerical/operator test and matched three-arm pilot.

SCORE: branch_lorentz_prefix | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=1 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: branch_lorentz_prefix | IN_SCOPE | Train-only successor entropy controls Lorentz radial coordinates used in code assignment, with behavior also entering the first-three-prefix closure; both are part of a connected pathway.
EVIDENCE: branch_lorentz_prefix | E1 E2 E5 E12 E13 E14 E15 E16 E6 E7
OBJECTION: branch_lorentz_prefix | The specification does not define how the per-item radial coordinate, prefix-specific Lorentz Frechet mean, and behavior-weighted prototype mean are made compatible with residual quantization or kept on the Lorentz manifold.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: branch_lorentz_prefix | If a group has one item, its Frechet mean is that item's target; if the behavior-weighted prototype is not constrained to the same point, Lclose can pull prototypes away from reconstruction without adding any within-group continuation information.
RATIONALE: branch_lorentz_prefix | E5 measures a successor entropy gradient, but does not show this entropy predicts useful branching conditional on assigned prefix; behavior=3. Lorentz exp/distance and curved closure are explicit, but the scalar radial feature can also be appended in Euclidean space and no matched-control argument rules this out (geometry=3). The proposal differs computationally from the measured successor-geodesic and tangent-residual mechanisms (E6-E7), but cited-work/ledger comparison beyond those is absent (novelty=3). It identifies q3/prefix closure, T3/T4 and Stage3 as downstream observables (downstream=4). Controls and a keep/reject rule are present, but no precise falsifier for closure versus radial entropy is given (falsifiability=3). Lorentz Frechet mean and “normalized behaviour-weighted mean” lack weights, projection/normalization definition and gradient details; modulo-32 extension also aliases groups >32 (implementability=1). It probes a materially different radial-plus-closure failure mode (exploration=3). UNKNOWN: manifold mean/prototype definitions and group coverage; bounded check: specify a valid Lorentz implementation and unit-test one-item and multi-item groups before training.

SCORE: successor_tail_transport | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: successor_tail_transport | IN_SCOPE | Train-only directed successor distributions form a tangent barycentre that is subtracted before Lorentz level-3 assignment; removing either behavior or curvature changes the assignment pathway.
EVIDENCE: successor_tail_transport | E1 E2 E5 E12 E13 E14 E15 E16 E6 E7
OBJECTION: successor_tail_transport | Successor targets’ current third codes are detached but nonstationary, so the transport direction may chase a moving codebook and erase semantic residual information rather than encode a stable branch discriminator.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: successor_tail_transport | If all observed successors have the same third code, their log-map barycentre equals that code direction for every source; the transport can shift all such sources identically and add no successor discrimination.
RATIONALE: successor entropy and top-successor mass are measured in E5, but the relevant code-conditioned barycentre signal is not measured, hence behavior=3. Tangent log/exp, clipping and Lorentz distance genuinely enter assignment; a matched Euclidean counterpart is mentioned but necessity and cancellation are not argued (geometry=3). The transport direction is computationally distinct from measured tangent successor residual and successor-geodesic coarse methods, though the family is close and prior-art search is unchecked (E6-E7; novelty=3). It specifies q3, prefix closure, T3/T4 and Stage3 outcomes (downstream=4). Both ablations and observable criteria are given, but a concrete falsifier and discriminating diagnostic are not fully specified (falsifiability=3). Sparse sampling and clipping are stated, yet prototype initialization, prefix representative construction, and numerical guards for Lorentz log at non-origin points remain incomplete (implementability=2). A negative would inform whether detached code-target transport is stable, so exploration=3. UNKNOWN: exact prefix representative and control matching; bounded check: gradient/numerical tests plus fixed-seed ablation on a small training run.

SCORE: branch_gate_curved_prefix | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: branch_gate_curved_prefix | IN_SCOPE | Training-only successor entropy sets item curvature for Lorentz level-3 assignment, while train transitions define a prefix continuation margin; both affect the first-three-code pathway.
EVIDENCE: branch_gate_curved_prefix | E1 E2 E5 E12 E13 E14 E15 E16 E6 E7
OBJECTION: branch_gate_curved_prefix | The curvature parameter changes both the distance geometry and potentially the scale of distances across items, but the specification does not normalize or calibrate costs across heterogeneous k_i; assignment may reflect scale artifacts rather than branching structure.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: branch_gate_curved_prefix | If all candidate distances for one item are multiplied by a positive item-specific constant, its argmin code is unchanged; thus curvature variation that only rescales distances has no assignment effect, despite being behavior-conditioned.
RATIONALE: branch entropy has measured stratification in E5, but no evidence establishes its connection to branch utility within the assigned prefix, so behavior=3. Lorentz distance/exp map are explicit and used, but matched Euclidean control is only named and the curvature-scale cancellation is not ruled out (geometry=3). This is a curvature-conditioned variant of the measured successor-geodesic and tangent-residual family (E6-E7); computationally distinct but near-family and no traceable external prior-art assessment (novelty=3). It names q3, continuation survival, teacher-forced accuracy and Stage3 outcome (downstream=4). Three conditions and outcomes are described, but the falsifier/threshold and diagnostic to isolate curvature from margin are weak (falsifiability=3). Core operators are implementable in principle, but curvature convention, cross-curvature distance comparability, and fixed-slot overflow behavior need clarification (implementability=2). A clear test of whether heteroscedastic curvature helps is useful even if negative (exploration=3). UNKNOWN: curvature calibration/control details; bounded check: compare per-item distance distributions and assignment changes against a matched Euclidean/scaled-distance control.

SCORE: transition_balanced_curved_residual | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: transition_balanced_curved_residual | IN_SCOPE | Train-only incoming popularity changes Sinkhorn row masses and transition edges define prefix balance; Lorentz geodesic costs jointly determine the level-3 transport assignment.
EVIDENCE: transition_balanced_curved_residual | E1 E2 E5 E12 E13 E14 E15 E16 E6 E7
OBJECTION: transition_balanced_curved_residual | The specified Sinkhorn row masses sum to one while column capacities sum to one, but each item’s hard argmax discards its transported mass; minibatch-local capacity balancing may not deliver the claimed global transition-aware code allocation.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: transition_balanced_curved_residual | With B=1, the row mass is 1 but each of 256 column capacities is 1/256; no feasible transport matrix can satisfy both marginals, so the proposed minibatch Sinkhorn is infeasible unless batch/capacity normalization is changed.
RATIONALE: transition entropy evidence in E5 supports nonuniform successor structure, but the proposed incoming-popularity weights and coverage are not measured directly, limiting behavior=3. Lorentz distances drive the transport cost and assignment; Euclidean control is specified, but there is no argument ruling out matched Euclidean costs or transport effects independent of curvature (geometry=3). This differs from measured coarse geodesic/tangent residual approaches (E6-E7) by using behavior-weighted transport, but external prior-art/ledger tracing is absent (novelty=3). It names assignment changes, successor-mass balance, T3/T4 diagnostics and Stage3 (downstream=4). Ablations and a keep criterion are specified, but no fully matched implementation or diagnostic isolating transport from geometry is provided (falsifiability=3). Sinkhorn is implementable in principle, yet the marginal feasibility issue, use of soft assignments in the RQ-VAE objective, and prefix sibling mass definition require repair (implementability=2). It is a substantially different assignment mechanism whose infeasibility/mini-batch mismatch would be informative (exploration=3). UNKNOWN: exact batch marginal normalization and soft-to-hard gradient; bounded check: verify row/column feasibility for actual batch sizes and quantify global versus minibatch code masses before full training.
EOF
